Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – MAY 6, 2021
A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on May 6, 2021 via
Zoom. Chairman Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.
Roll Call
Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, - Commissioner 1
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District 2
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District 3
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Juan Mata, Parks Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  None
Public Comments

  None
Approval of the Minutes
  Commissioner Denmon made a clarification regarding the spelling of his name.
Commissioner Beck made a motion to approve the minutes from April 1, 2021. Commissioner
McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  Nays: None
Staff Report
  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement with Bateman
Community Living LLC dba TRIO Community Meals in the amount of $304,243.25 for the provision
of breakfast, lunch, and snacks for the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer
Food Service Program (SFSP) from May 3, 2021 through August 31, 2021 (CDE Grant Fund).
  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Denmon seconded. The motion was approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – MAY 6, 2021
Verbal Reports

  Juan Mata gave a verbal report on behalf of Parks Administration regarding the following:
    The Graffiti Crew continues to abate graffiti in all four (4) districts. The month of April had an
  unusual occurrence of incidents on personal property (cars) and residential property (homes,
  front doors and garages). Incidents at North Park have escalated. Our goal is to have the
  graffiti removed within 24 hours from notice or reports.
    The Park Maintenance staff installed 7,500 square feet of sod on March 4th around the newly
  renovated restrooms at Rogers Park. They also planted nine (9) 60-inch box trees in
  collaboration with the SoFi Stadium personnel at Vincent Park.
  Commissioner Beck asked if there was known knowledge of specific locations the graffiti
was happening or is it throughout the four (4) districts. Director Barnes stated that the concentration
of that graffiti was specifically in District 4 along 110th Street intersecting Lemoli Avenue.
Commissioner Beck asked if these incidents occurred on a specific day. Director Barnes stated they
occurred during the week, at night and was discovered the following morning. The Graffiti Abatement
team was informed and arrived at the location accompanied by the Inglewood Police for the removal.
Commissioner Beck asked have there been any more incidents since. Director Barnes stated there
have not been any further incidents. She also stated that in recent weeks there’s reason to believe
that neighboring individuals have been coming into our community defacing property. Commissioner
Denmon asked what role does the Parks and Recreation Department or Graffiti Abatement play in
the removal of graffiti on private property. Director Barnes stated due to the nature of this particular
incident, the Graffiti Abatement team acted by removing the graffiti, but generally do not address
public property. If deemed a public safety issue we’re given authorization to act in removing the
graffiti. Typically, this particular type of tagging could initiate or lead to other activities in the area
which is why we’re given special permission to remove the graffiti to the extent allowed. The Graffiti
Abatement’s role is to try and remove graffiti within 24-hours depending on the activity in the area.
Some areas experience more graffiti than others and during the summer there seems to always be
an escalation of graffiti.
  Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Summer Camp Updates: Summer Day Camp in past practices was offered at Rogers, Darby
  and Simiski Parks. Due to COVID-19 our practices have changed. Adhering to the Public
  Health Department and L.A. County guidelines and things unfolding daily, we had to modify
  our schedule to operating at a 50% capacity and offering Summer Camp at Rogers and
  Darby Parks. Camp will be held Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Darby Park
  has experienced a low registration rate of five (5) kids which was understandable because
  parents may not be comfortable with having their children enrolled due to the pandemic. The
  children that were enrolled at Rogers Park may have resulted due to lack of child care.
  Similar to last year, due to COVID-19 we will be operating with some protocol modifications
  for Summer Camp. Summer Camp will be offered at Rogers and Darby Parks. The operating
  hours will be 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday. The fee for Inglewood residents is

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – MAY 6, 2021
  $110.00, per session and $203.00 per session for Non Residents. The sessions run two (2)
  consecutive weeks with a total of four (4) sessions available beginning June 21 until August
  13, 2021. This schedule coincides with the Inglewood Unified School District’s schedule.
  Summer Camp was really fun last year, the children still had a great time. We were able to
  offer virtual field trips. Registration will be available for 50 kids at Rogers and 40 kids at
  Darby Park. We will continue to adhere to social distancing guidelines. This year we will be
  adding additional instructors to do more individual activities with the groups including Zumba
  and Dance Classes. Each individual child will receive a personal packet of essential tools
  needed for camp. Summer Camp is for ages 3 through 12. Registration began May 3rd.
  The Edward Vincent, Jr. Park Swim Complex is very popular during the summer season
  opening in June and closing on Labor Day. This year we will be offering a variety of swim
  lessons. General swim hours are 12:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. and pre-registration is required.
  Vincent Park’s pool opens June 16th will swim lessons beginning on June 23rd. and the pool
  closes on September 6, 2021 Swimming Registration will begin on May 10th.
  The Parks Recreation Centers remain closed.
  Center Park offers self-defense classes which met capacity the first week of registration for
  the month of May.
  Zumba classes have started on the outdoor patio section at Rogers Park. Classes began
  May 1st on Wednesdays from 6:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. and Saturday’s 9:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m.
  during the month of May. Beginning in June, classes will be held on Tuesdays from 6:30
  p.m. to 7:30 p.m. and Saturday’s from 9:30 a.m. to10:30 a.m.
  On Saturday May 15, 2021, we will be offering a free water safety workshop. On the city’s
  social media platform, myths are being submitted daily. The first 100 people who register
  and attend will receive a giveaway bag. The workshop will be virtual. Bags include safety
  water tips and other water related essentials. Great for the entire family the workshop will be
  from 10:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. Pre-Registration is required and available online at
  www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org as well as www.cityofinglewood.org under the
  Departments page.
  The Recreation Division is also offering Family Paint Days beginning Saturday, May 22nd.
  each class is an hour and a half. The first class will be held at Rogers Park, the second on
  June 19th at Edward Vincent, Jr Park, and the last class will be conducted on Saturday, July
  24th at Darby Park. All classes are outdoors for $10.00 per person, ages 5 and up with a
  maximum of 25 participants.
  Dodgers RBI has started for kid’s ages 5 to 18. The City has partnered with the Los Angeles
  Dodgers Foundation for the last four (4) to five (5) years. This year there will be no
  registration fees. Children will be provided with uniforms for both home and away games,
  bats, gloves, balls and other tools needed to play baseball. Other components of the
  program include education, virtual workshops for parents, college tours for children and
  fitness clinics will be available. Registration is available online on the city’s website.
  This year marks the 72nd Annual Memorial Day celebration which will be held virtually via
  the city’s Facebook page. It will be live Monday, May 31st, air time will be announced and

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – MAY 6, 2021
  provided. All the information is available in the Community Information Guide and available
  on the city’s website.
  Commissioner Denmon thanked Ms. Estrada for her report and stated it’s good to see the
programs are back up and running. Sabrina Barnes informed the Commissioners that the hardcopies
of the Community Information Guides will be available beginning Monday, May 10, 2021. Ms.
Maldonado will send the electronic versions out on May 7th. The guide was drafted prior to the orange
tier restrictions opening up and may change as full reopening officially occurs on June 15, 2021. We
are still operating under the current guidelines in terms of indoor facilities and numbers allowed. She
stated the Senior Center remains closed. Our leadership hasn’t given any guidelines regarding
special events. We are proceeding with caution and technically still working remotely. Future events
could be held hybrid and at some point in person but as of current there is no certainty. We’re
currently hiring right now for part-time Recreation Leaders, Lifeguards, and Recreation Aides,
applicants can apply via the city’s website www.cityofinglewood.org or contact our Human Resources
Department.
  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Friday, April 23, 2021, Parks, Recreation and Community Services along with the Office of
  Emergency held a successful vaccination clinic. 140 people attended and received their first
  dose of the COVID-19
   Vaccine at the Inglewood senior center. Vaccinations were administered by the Apex Care
  home health pharmacy. The second (2) Dose will be administered Friday May 14th 2021. In
  total 230 people were vaccinated at the Inglewood Senior Center.
   Senior meals are still in high demand and are cooked fresh daily, approximately 500 seniors
  receive about 3500 meals on a weekly basis. Fresh produce is sourced in collaboration with
  the social justice institute and monthly boxes are delivered in collaboration with the Los
  Angeles Food Bank.
   Our senior and disable Transportation Program continues to provide senior trips to dialysis,
  and medical appointments that are necessary. Drivers are receiving additional training on
  the most up to date COVID-19 practices and advance defensive driving techniques. Mask
  are required for both the driver and passengers. Supplies needed such as mask or hand
  sanitizer is an available upon request.
   The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) will start July 14th through August 20th 2021.
  Youth 18 years or younger may visit Darby, Rogers, Siminski or Lock Haven Parks between
  the hours of 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. to receive breakfast and lunch. Vincent, North, Ashwood
  Parks, the Inglewood Library and Crenshaw Library provide lunches and snacks between
  the hours of 12 p.m. to 2 p.m.
  Commissioner Denmon thanked Mr. Devlia and stated the programs have been very
successful.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – MAY 6, 2021
  Director Barnes stated there is a Little Library located at North Park. She has been
approached by a non-profit organization who is interested in placing additional Little Libraries at nine
(9) city parks. Little Libraries are little cabinets that range from 3 feet by 1 foot to standing as high as
6 feet tall and 3 feet wide. Children and the general public can come and grab a book and read while
visiting the park or take the book home and return it later. The Little Library is a shared space for
books and is meant to promote literacy. We’ve received a proposal and it’s anticipated we will allow
a pilot of two (2) sites to ensure they are a fit for the other parks and that they are maintained. The
libraries will need to be stocked and if vandalized they’ll need to be repaired. We will then make a
determination if we’ll continue with at the additional parks. As part of the Memorandum of
Understanding (MOU), they will ensure the facility is properly maintained and have an evaluation of
the pilot period. Commissioner Fragoso asked will the maintenance include the library located at
North Park. Director Barnes stated yes, we can request that the group be responsible for the
maintenance at North Park. Commissioner Beck asked Commissioner Fragoso has the library been
a good experience. Commissioner Fragoso stated it is a positive experience for the children. Director
Barnes stated some of the Little Libraries are a part of the Rotary Club in concentrated
neighborhoods. Commissioner Beck stated having a child of 8 years of age that likes to play video
games, reading a book it is imperative. Commissioner Denmon thanked Director Barnes and stated
he hopes the pilot programs shows the organization will maintain and stock the books.
  Director Barnes stated staff is about a week into the budget preparation for the next fiscal
year and we are to maintain a status quo. If there are things that need to be addressed we may
revisit them after the start of the new fiscal year.
Commissioners Comments
  Commissioner Denmon commented that he hopes when the Willie Agee Playhouse reopens
he is able to do a walk through. Director Barnes stated Shelli Boone, Playhouse Manager is aware
and will have staff available when needed to access the Playhouse.
  Commissioner Denmon wished all the mothers a Happy Mother’s Day.
  Commissioner Beck thanked the Commissioner’s for welcoming him and thanked Director
Barnes and staff for all the reports given this evening.
  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:39 p.m.
